units.text: INT. SUPERMAN - CONTINUOUS
querulously.

There now! put it on me, of course. I never thought of it until Tavy told me she said I did. But, you know, I'm very fond of Tavy: he's a sort of son to me; and I don't want him to be trampled on and made wretched.
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: Whereas I don't matter, I suppose.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Oh, you are different, somehow: you are able to take care of yourself. You'd serve her out. And anyhow, she must marry somebody.
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: Aha! there speaks the life instinct. You detest her; but you feel that you must get her married.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: rising, shocked.
Do you mean that I detest my own daughter! Surely you don't believe me to be so wicked and unnatural as that, merely because I see her faults.
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: cynically.
You love her, then?
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Why, of course I do. What queer things you say, Jack! We can't help loving our own blood relations.
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: Well, perhaps it saves unpleasantness to say so. But for my part, I suspect that the tables of consanguinity have a natural basis in a natural repugnance
units.name: TANNER

units.text: he rises.

You shouldn't say things like that, Jack. I hope you won't tell Ann that I have been speaking to you. I only wanted to set myself right with you and Tavy. I couldn't sit mumchance and have everything put on me.
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: politely.
Quite so.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: dissatisfied.

And now I've only made matters worse. Tavy's angry with me because I don't worship Ann. And when it's been put into my head that Ann ought to marry you, what can I say except that it would serve her right?
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: Thank you.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Now don't be silly and twist what I say into something I don't mean. I ought to have fair play--
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: Ann comes from the villa, followed presently by Violet, who is dressed for driving.
coming to her mother's right hand with threatening suavity.
Well, mamma darling, you seem to be having a delightful chat with Jack. We can hear you all over the place.
units.name: ANN

units.text: appalled.
Have you overheard--
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: Never fear: Ann is only--well, we were discussing that habit of hers just now. She hasn't heard a word.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: stoutly.
I don't care whether she has or not: I have a right to say what I please.
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: arriving on the lawn and coming between Mrs Whitefield and Tanner.
I've come to say goodbye. I'm off for my honeymoon.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: crying.
Oh don't say that, Violet. And no wedding, no breakfast, no clothes, nor anything.
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: petting her.
It won't be for long.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: Don't let him take you to America. Promise me that you won't.
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: very decidedly.
I should think not, indeed. Don't cry, dear: I'm only going to the hotel.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: But going in that dress, with your luggage, makes one realize--
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: she chokes, and then breaks out again.
How I wish you were my daughter, Violet!
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: soothing her.
There, there: so I am. Ann will be jealous.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: Ann doesn't care a bit for me.
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: Fie, mother! Come, now: you mustn't cry any more: you know Violet doesn't like it
units.name: ANN

units.text: Mrs Whitefield dries her eyes, and subsides.
Goodbye, Jack.
units.name: VIOLET
